text: First written record, as Vyzaka, in a royal charter for the provostry of Lelesz.
First written record, as Scinna: the king gives the village to Jakov, county head of Uzhhorod.
A parish is on record.
First written record, as Solmus, in a charter of King Sigismund.
Senné has at least 25 serf households, Iňačovce at least 19.
23 serf households, and a curia of the Dobó family.
Senné: 26 serf houses, a manor, a church and a rectory. Iňačovce: 32 serf houses.
Rákóczi's rising. The Latin parishes of the county have to be rebuilt afterwards, Senné among them.
Plague. The tax list of 1715 finds 8 households (PL-E-001).
Tax census: 5 households in Senné, 8 in Iňačovce.
Roman Catholic church rebuilt on old foundations.
Tax census: 11 households in each village. After this Iňačovce is refilled from the north of Ung and Zemplín.
List of parishes, then the bishop of Eger's visitation. Senné is a Latin parish with eight filials. Iňačovce has its own Greek Catholic parish, where Rusyn is spoken.
Reformed register begins.
Urbarial survey: 26 villein households in Senné, 35 in Iňačovce. Baron István Vécsey is the main landlord of both.
Greek Catholic eparchy of Mukachevo erected; the bishop sits at Uzhhorod.

The official list of settlements puts Szenna and Solymos in the Szobránc district and gives Solymos a parish of the Greek rite. It also gave each village a main language; that column has not been read for either.
The parish survey lists a Greek Catholic mother church at Bölzse with Gönyű and Szina among its filials.
A water mill on an arm of the Uh is first recorded.
Vályi's gazetteer: Szenna has several lords and Catholic inhabitants; Solymos and both Szeretvas are its filials.
The Roman Catholic parishes of Ung county pass from Eger to the new diocese of Szatmár.
Its Greek Catholics move from the Bežovce parish to the Čičarovce parish, where they stay until the 1940s.

The Mukachevo eparchy counts its people settlement by settlement and records the language of the sermon: Rusyn in 1,276 settlements, Hungarian in 346, Romanian in 180, Slovak in 41. The entry for the parish of Solymos has not been read.
Augustín Roškováni, later bishop of Vác and of Nitra, is born in the manor to an estate employee's family.
489 Roman Catholics in the village and 903 in the filials. A church tower is begun and collapses.
Greek Catholic register begins.
Land census: Senné 120 houses and 833 people; Iňačovce 119 houses and 1,023 people.
Surviving Roman Catholic register begins.
A Greek Catholic widow of Szenna dies on 17 August 'in cholera': the first time the disease is named in a register of these villages.
The bishop of Szatmár's circulars are copied into a parish book: the Duska agent's Folder 1.
Serfdom abolished. In Senné each holding keeps about 13 hectares; labour dues for forest and pasture run on until the 1896 buy-out law.
Fényes's gazetteer: 580 Roman Catholics, 238 Greek Catholics, 22 Jews, 3 Reformed, 2 Lutherans.
Fényes calls Solymos a Rusyn, Slovak and Hungarian village, Rusyn first.
Schools: Roman Catholic in Senné, 61 pupils. Greek Catholic, 69 pupils, and Reformed, 14 pupils, in Iňačovce.
A fire on 28 October, set 'by a malicious man' by the parish's own record. The surviving baptism book begins the next year.
First full census of Hungary. The Ung county sheets are now at Berehove.
First wave of emigration.
Cholera in the Greek Catholic parish: three burials in a row at Jesztreb in August. It had killed at Viszoka in December 1872.
A flood in May; a girl of Solymos drowns, and the priest writes 'the flood of the year 1874' beside her burial.
Ján Csurgovics becomes Greek Catholic parish priest, after Jozef Kubek (1847-1881). He serves to 1886.
State civil registration begins on 1 October.
A state registry office opens and has sat in the village ever since. Its district takes in Vysoká nad Uhom.
Szenna becomes Ungszenna in the official renaming. 754 people: 484 Roman Catholic, 231 Greek Catholic.
Renamed Magasrév by the Hungarian place-name law; another source says the old name ran to 1899.
A birth at Solymos is entered by the state registrar at Alsókánya (Jastrabie).
Lightning burns the church roof. The church is then lengthened and vaulted.
Second wave of emigration, mostly to the United States. Many return to buy land.
By mother tongue at the census, Slovak is the largest group in both villages, as a later map drawn from the returns shows.
The Reformed build their own church.
Solymos, with 885 people, is in the notary district of Alsókánya (Jastrabie).
Treaty of Trianon, 4 June. The villages are in Czechoslovakia; the names Senné and Iňačovce become official.
Land reform begins to break up the Vécsey estate. Iňačovce is placed in the Michalovce district.
Baron László Vécsey dies; the estate passes to his nephew Mihály Sztáray.
Stráňany, the Sztrajnyán of a baptism strip of about 1887, is joined to the town.
The slump hits the farms that had mortgaged themselves to buy estate land.
Lightning on 6 July 1929 and a fire on 1 April 1930 damage the Greek Catholic church archive.
Czechoslovak census, by household and house number.
Census of 1 December: 161 houses, 169 households, 754 people. The summary is signed at Palín.
A death of 18 August is noted in the Greek Catholic baptism volume for 1870-1898: the old book is still in use.
Mobilisation in September. On 2 November the First Vienna Award returns Uzhhorod to Hungary.
Ceded to Hungary in November with the Veľké Kapušany district. Belža, Gyňov and Seňa, south of Košice, go the same month.
Little War, 23 to 31 March. Slovak volunteers hold Senné; an air fight is seen over the village. The new border runs about 2 km away.
Protocol of 4 April: the border follows the boundary of Senné with Bežovce and of Iňačovce with Blatná Polianka and Blatné Remety. Handed over on 7 April.
Senné: 171 houses, 839 people. Iňačovce: 190 houses, 747 people. About 600 cows die in Senné and harvests fail until 1942.
The church chronicle records hunger: "Niet nieže chleba, ale ani zemiakov" (not only no bread, not even potatoes).
Register of Jews: 20 people in Senné, 13 in Iňačovce. Four families are deported from Senné.
Hungarian then German troops in the village from 28 October; fields flooded; a machine-gun post in the church tower. Soviet soldiers enter on 27 November.
Czechoslovakia restored. Uzhhorod and the eastern part of old Ung county pass to the Soviet Union.
The manor is nationalised by decree of 27 November; from 1946 it is the school.
Becomes a Greek Catholic parish of its own on 26 September, after provisional status from 1945.
The Senné fishponds reserve is declared, in the fields of Iňačovce and Senné.
Farm cooperative founded on 30 January, the last in the district.
Moved from the Veľké Kapušany district to Michalovce.
The Rusyn language is given a written standard in Slovakia on 27 January. Rusyn is a recognised national minority there.
